limitations: Agentic remains WIP and absent from default supported BOM/independent consumers.

Completed async outputs and controlled-suspended async consumer snapshots have Java 8 cross-JVM acceptance; arbitrary crash points, planner in-flight rescheduling and ordinary async failure history still need acceptance.
Terminal-stream recovery, global cancellation and remaining complex Agentic behavior are pending.
Resume is method-level re-entry for unfinished consumers, not arbitrary Java stack continuation.
Cross-process tests use single-writer file fixtures and orderly suspended exits; no claim of multi-writer atomicity or external-side-effect exactly-once delivery.
All 51 baseline main Test classes execute on JDK 17; external-model IT suite remains unrun.
Loopback fixtures do not prove real remote interoperability.
Async normalization covers top-level scope values and invocation output; user containers with nested runtime Future values are not validated.

Patterns remains WIP and outside supported BOM/independent consumers; seven pattern foundation paths do not prove full policies, model routing/extraction, async/streaming, lifecycle, cancellation or persistence.
The eight unchanged baseline patterns Test classes run on JDK 17; service IT and full end-to-end scenarios remain pending.
Agentic MCP/A2A, remaining main Agentic, broader MCP/model/vector work and final delivery remain pending.
Streaming pattern test uses synthetic StreamingChatModel callbacks and an owned emitter executor, not HTTP/SSE interoperability.

Voting recovery tests use String memory IDs, a single-writer file fixture and orderly suspended exits; arbitrary crash points/multi-writer atomicity/external side-effect exactly-once execution remain unproven.

Debate recovery covers normal suspended exits with a single-writer/String-ID file fixture; arbitrary crash points, multi-writer atomicity and external side-effect exactly-once execution remain unproven.
Earlier WIP Debate checkpoints without complete round/judge fields are outside the new-format recovery claim.
Full task/network-stream cancellation, complete ordinary-failure history persistence/automatic retry and all broader pending scope remain incomplete.
Failure cleanup does not impose a new asynchronous timeout contract on user-provided synchronous persistence/listener implementations.
Interrupt-ignoring user code cannot be forcibly stopped. Scope-method guards do not cover direct writes through the exposed state() Map or external side effects.

Inline/single-thread caller executors retain their own scheduling constraints; no preemption while Executor.execute itself blocks. Root cancellation still depends on cooperative interruption and framework scope-method boundaries.

Blocking synchronous persistence, listener, ChatMemory providers or DeferredResponse completion callbacks are not given a new bounded cancellation contract; scope guard lock boundaries need further audit.

Physical cancellation is verified for default OkHttp and framework-consumed intermediate streams; terminal TokenStream, custom providers/transports, arbitrary asynchronous tool executors remain pending. Default OkHttp explicitly captured callbacks now restore the scope guard generation; not every Agentic ThreadLocal is restored.
Successful-call cleanup for overwritten tasks, complete ordinary-failure history/automatic retry, callback/guard lock boundaries and the full Agentic/MCP/model/vector/BOM scope remain incomplete.

Scope-generation guards are proven for explicitly captured contexts and default OkHttp callbacks; arbitrary custom transports, asynchronous tool executors and user-created threads still need propagation/acceptance. Direct state() Map mutations and external side effects remain outside these scope-method guards.

The late-tool fixture half-closes server output to trigger SSE EOF and tool execution; its EOF is not independent evidence that root cancellation closed a pre-EOF request. Earlier seven physical cancellation fixtures retain their separate assertions.

Configured AI Services tool/completion executor seams now carry the captured owner and provider context. Arbitrary custom implementations, user-created threads and callbacks not using these seams still require acceptance.

Queued tasks become no-ops and clear their captured references; arbitrary caller executor queue entries are not physically purged. cancel(false) preserves running ownership until completion/root cancellation.
Provider cleanup Error after publication reaches executor uncaught-error channel and does not replace already published result.
The focused core helper API audit proves only CapturedContextSupport; it is not a full core baseline comparison.
Root cancellation is verified for cancellable provider CompletableFuture. Arbitrary provider I/O which ignores cancel(true) cannot be forcibly terminated.
This increment restores the cancellation owner and its guard generation for framework downstream notifications; it does not propagate every user ThreadLocal to arbitrary provider-created threads.
Future cancellation may synchronously invoke arbitrary provider/user callbacks. This increment does not add a bounded timeout contract for blocking callbacks or force-stop uncooperative user code.
Explicit compensation mode drains already-started tools before rollback, preserving the fixed-baseline contract; it does not force-stop unknown external side effects.

Cancellation of non-cooperative provider I/O, arbitrary CompletionStage/third-party adapters and blocking inline executors/callbacks is not guaranteed. Native annotated CompletableFuture is tested, not every external adapter.
Reactive cleanup failures are logged while cancellation proceeds for remaining tools; a cancelled subscription receives no additional terminal signal.

Two-tool fixtures exercise concurrent pending asynchronous work on a borrowed single-worker executor and controlled reversed completion. They do not exhaust arbitrary fan-out counts, schedulers or external side effects.
Refusing provider Future remains pending until provider/user cleanup completes it; diagnostics do not force-stop I/O.
Explicit completionResponseProcessingExecutor parameter path is verified; no new high-level AiServices builder option was added.
Model HTTP/SSE normally completed before cancelling completion processing in these fixtures. Its normal EOF is not evidence of root-driven network cancellation.

runWithOwner restores captured cancellation owner when present, preserving existing caller behavior when absent. It does not reapply every user ExecutorProvider ThreadLocal for a cancelled-task error callback.
Blocking error handlers, inline executors and interruption-ignoring providers have no new forced-stop/timeout contract.
Terminal output retains caller-controlled consumption and error handling; no automatic replay of returned workflows or tool requests was added.
Captured cancellation owner is restored at start; arbitrary user ThreadLocals, non-cooperative custom SDKs/transports and user-created threads are outside this proof.
Post-drain single-terminal evidence applies to OpenAI Chat Completions callback SSE. Responses API and other model integrations retain their separate pending business acceptance.

These new boundary fixtures use registered resource probes, not third-party I/O. Existing actual HTTP/SSE coverage remains in the full clean; all external/custom component lifecycle semantics are not proven.

Scope creation tests use registered-resource probes, single-call store failures and controlled reentrant replacement. Arbitrary concurrent initialization, distributed-store transactions and external/custom I/O require separate proof.

A store may write then throw; no delete, write retry or distributed rollback is inferred. Persistent/registered scopes surviving a creation listener failure retain failed state for explicit inspection; creation listener is not promised to replay on the next call.

Synchronous Future tool waiting intentionally now responds to interruption by cancelling the raw Future and throwing CancellationException instead of waiting uninterruptibly/converting cancellation to error text.

Cancellation cannot roll back external side effects or force-stop interruption-ignoring providers/inline blocking executors. Arbitrary third-party CompletionStage adapters and full custom transport semantics remain pending.

Saved-handle coverage proves default OpenAI/OkHttp serial callbacks and controlled tool/executor scheduling. Arbitrary concurrent custom SDK callbacks, non-cooperative blocking cancellation/listener code and all scheduler races remain unproven.

Manual flow cancellation does not mark parent root cancelled and cannot force-stop already-running external side effects. An in-progress user callback/provider can continue if it refuses interruption.

Normal ownership-detach failures are logged while remaining resources are detached; no second terminal is sent. Cancellation failures remain caller diagnostics; stream-error cleanup failures are suppressed on primary.

Drain covers framework-registered async and consumed intermediate-stream completions; arbitrary user-created unregistered Futures, external late scheduling and concurrent roots for one scope need separate proof.
Controlled pause/recovery is retained in current regression suites; arbitrary crash points and complete failed-history durability are not claimed by this runtime-only tracker.

Three public methods were added to compatibility @Internal InvocationTasks; fixed official-baseline visible classes gained no new declarations in this increment. One private Computation class was added.
All four Agentic modules, remaining MCP/model/vector integrations and BOM/consumer/final-delivery scope remain incomplete.

scope_added: 7 native Java8 child processes prove overwritten async success waits before notification, early/late ordinary failures fail root, sibling failure cancels pending computation, next root does not reconsume prior failure, external marker remains caller-owned and recovered error is not rethrown.

2 native Java8 loopback OpenAI/OkHttp SSE children prove overwritten non-async consumed intermediate streams also wait for success/error; replacement state preserved, one request, socket/error release and dispatcher drain checked before fixture cleanup.
Existing controlled pause/recovery, deferred state, asynchronous planning/failure cleanup and lazy terminal stream acceptance retained; no caller-owned terminal model started by drain.
behavior_change: Framework-owned computations are tracked before dispatch, independently of final state key values. Both AsyncResponse and AgentExecutor consumed RecoverableStream register completion signals with the root generation.

Root barrier precedes success notification. Ordinary failure signal wakes the barrier without waiting for unrelated pending siblings, then existing root failure cleanup cancels owned work. Controlled suspension is retained and settled old pause records are retired on resume.

Standard error recovery remains inside supplier/stream recovery; successful recovered values are not rethrown. External PendingResponse values are not completed/cancelled by the barrier. No automatic supplier/tool replay, checkpoint schema or production dependency change.
